question: Should verified consumption by the requester permanently satisfy a descendant completion's delivery obligation even when the requester's final outward delivery subsequently fails?
rationale: The code can enforce either boundary, but source and tests cannot determine whether the product contract ends at child-to-requester consumption or requires eventual user-visible requester delivery.

options.title: Credit requester consumption
options.body: Treat explicit requester adoption as terminal descendant delivery proof, while the requester owns any later outward-delivery recovery.

options.title: Require outward success
options.body: Keep descendants retryable until the composed requester result reaches its final delivery target, accepting possible duplicate descendant handling.

options.title: Fold into durable inbox
options.body: Pause this mechanism and address the boundary through the broader durable completion inbox tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/67777.

recommendation.title: Credit requester consumption
recommendation.body: Treat explicit requester adoption as terminal descendant delivery proof, while the requester owns any later outward-delivery recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on the current subagent announcement and registry lifecycle surfaces makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the delivery-boundary decision.
